clue.text: Plagued with obstinacy

definitions.meaning: plagued means pursued or troubled persistently, as by a hound on one's heels
with obstinacy describes a tenacious, stubborn manner

explanation.surface: Someone troubled by their own stubbornness.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dogged is to be followed persistently by trouble, and a dogged person shows stubborn persistence.

clue.text: Covering 5dn, perhaps, that's lost a leading character

parts.note: the answer to 5 down is an example of an opera

indicators.note: losing a leading character means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: that's gives the word that, the possessive adding nothing

explanation.surface: A hat for an opera-goer is missing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hat is a collapsible top hat, a head covering for the theatre.

clue.text: American of the 18th century

definitions.meaning: a person from the US state of Georgia
belonging to the reigns of the four King Georges, 1714 to 1830

explanation.surface: Describing a colonial-era American.
explanation.walkthrough: The Georgian period is the era of Britain's Kings George I to IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A Georgian can be a native of the US state of Georgia, and the Georgian era in Britain spanned the 18th century.

clue.text: Excellent person, a beauty, we hear, the object of a proposal

parts.note: a daisy is old slang for a first-rate person or thing

indicators.note: we hear says the word for a beauty is spoken

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A wonderful, lovely woman is the one a man asks to marry him.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Bell is the old song 'Daisy, Daisy, give me your answer do', a marriage proposal on a bicycle built for two.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's singer asks Daisy for her hand, so she is the woman being asked to wed.

clue.text: Fine worker a small amount

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm or a ship
some means a modest quantity

explanation.surface: A good labourer is paid only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means fine or good-looking, and also generous, as in a fine sum.

clue.text: Merry England's the real opera

indicators.note: merry suggests tipsy and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A claim that 'Merry England' is the genuine opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry England' is itself the name of a comic opera, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Humperdinck's work based on the fairy tale is a well-known opera.

clue.text: Decree the overthrow of foreign state police

indicators.note: overthrow turns everything that follows upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: etat is French for state
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: An order to topple a foreign regime's secret police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the overthrow of' turns ETAT plus CID backwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to lay down with authority, like issuing an order.

clue.text: Press too hard about Paddington

parts.note: over means about, concerning
Paddington is the famous fictional bear from Peru

explanation.surface: Journalists hound the famous bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists; it is a verb, to push.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbear is to dominate or overwhelm by weight or force.

clue.text: Departed with strain, two wickets gone — so dig in

indicators.note: W stands for wicket in cricket scoring, so two of them are removed

parts.note: went means departed
a wrench is a sprain or strain

explanation.surface: A batsman leaves injured after two wickets fall, so the team settles in.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrench is to dig trenches and establish a firm defensive position.

clue.text: Loyalty and love — it's around in part of England

indicators.note: in places the love-and-it group inside the county name

parts.note: Devon is a county in south-west England
love is zero in tennis, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: around turns the word it so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone's faithfulness and affection are rooted in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's around' reads as a phrase; 'around' instead turns the word it backwards, and 'in' sets that with the love letter inside the county.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion is steadfast attachment, the same quality as faithful loyalty.

clue.text: Bill has very little money — it could be grave

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be paid
a cent is a coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: Someone's bill is almost nothing, which might be a serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like serious; it is the grave mark over a letter, as in à.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is one kind of diacritic mark placed over a vowel, alongside acute and circumflex.

clue.text: Stern of leaking ship -see about something to carry the water away

definitions.text: something to carry the water away

indicators.note: the stern is a ship's rear, so the rear letter of leaking is taken

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

indicators.note: about turns the cathedral city round so it reads backwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Looking at the back of a leaky vessel, you hunt for a way to drain it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ELY, a see (bishop's seat) in Cambridgeshire, into YLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved spout on a building that throws rainwater clear of the walls.

clue.text: Cover the French doctor

parts.note: garb is clothing, what covers the body
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Concealing the identity of a French physician.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor a text is to falsify or distort it, which is what garbling does.

clue.text: Recess, when a vote turned in can be changed

indicators.note: in puts the turned vote inside the rearranged letters
changed tells us the letters of can be are rearranged
turned means the yes-vote is read backwards

parts.note: aye is a vote in favour, as in Parliament

explanation.surface: During a parliamentary break, a vote that has been reversed can be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes AYE into EYA, which goes 'in' ABNCE, the letters of CAN BE 'changed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyance is a state of temporary suspension, a recess or pause in activity.

clue.text: Protection misinterpreted in Malachi

indicators.note: a misinterpreted text has its letters read in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A passage in the book of Malachi about safety has been misread.
explanation.walkthrough: Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is armour of interlinked rings, worn as defence in battle.

clue.text: Hit for six, using bats the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for mad, as is nuts

explanation.surface: A cricketer smashes a six while holding the bat incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit for six' is cricket for a shot clearing the boundary, and also means to stun or shock; 'the wrong way' turns NUTS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hit for six is a British idiom for being utterly shocked or overwhelmed.

clue.text: "Barred" without small coin is "Bared"

indicators.note: without means outside, so barred surrounds the coin

parts.note: striped means marked with bars
P is a penny, a small British coin

explanation.surface: A grammar note that taking a coin from 'barred' leaves 'bared'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests removing letters; 'without' here means outside, putting P inside STRIPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped means laid bare, uncovered.

clue.text: Employing woman in work in a cinema

indicators.note: in places the woman word inside the employing word

parts.note: using means employing
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Hiring a woman for a job at the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers show patrons to their seats, a job done in theatres and picture houses.

clue.text: After a Catholic, Henry appears waggish

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry turns up playful after meeting a Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means mischievous and knowing, like a playful wag's manner.

clue.text: Weariest form, so to speak

indicators.note: form means shape the letters of weariest into something new

explanation.surface: The most tired shape, as it might be put.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase signals a figurative expression, in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Flirt takes the cake right away

indicators.note: away says the right letter is removed

parts.note: a croquette is a small cake of minced food, fried in breadcrumbs

explanation.surface: A flirtatious woman grabs the gateau and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the cake' looks like the idiom; it is just link plus cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette is a woman who flirts for amusement.

clue.text: Sunday best for making jokes about youth, right?

indicators.note: about means the jokes word goes around the youth and right

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: Wearing your finest clothes invites teasing about being a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are one's smartest clothes, worn for special occasions like Sunday church.

clue.text: Bachelor has not accepted change little by little

indicators.note: not says the accepted letter is left out

parts.note: a bachelor is a graduate, holder of a first degree
U means socially acceptable, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: An unmarried man refuses to adapt gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: U is upper-class British usage, 'acceptable', from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: To gradate is to pass by gradual stages from one shade or state to another.

clue.text: Some police capture a Pole

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Officers arrest a man from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is a geographic pole, by extension the frozen region there.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of Earth's poles is covered by a permanent sheet of ice, so the frozen polar region stands for it.

clue.text: To appear legitimate, state needs urgent reform

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

indicators.note: reform means the letters of urgent are reshaped

explanation.surface: A government wanting to seem lawful must urgently change its ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring true is to sound genuine or credible, like a sound coin.

clue.text: Particular chap first on the scene

parts.note: prim means fussy, particular about propriety
Al is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A fastidious man is the first to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means original or earliest, coming before all else.

clue.text: Take off a garment and go without

indicators.note: without means outside, so the go word surrounds the garment

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Removing an item of clothing and doing without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like undressing; it means a mocking imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a parody, and a travesty is a grotesque imitation of something.

clue.text: Bank beside the railway lines

parts.note: the Dogger Bank is a large sandbank in the North Sea
EL is the American elevated railway

explanation.surface: A grassy bank next to train tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like railway lines; it is lines of verse. DOGGER Bank is a North Sea shipping area.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is poor-quality comic verse, a set of rhyming lines.

clue.text: Before going in was first, I'd slyly say

indicators.note: going in means the word for before is placed inside

parts.note: led means was first, in front
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone recalls going in first, speaking slyly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is said aloud: 'I'd slyly' sounds like 'eyed slyly', which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a sly, suggestive way, i.e. to have eyed them slyly.
